paragraphs.source_en: The go-between who had been working back and forth between the two sides was none other than Kazumasa’s grandmother, the widow of Ishikawa Aki-no-kami Kiyokane. Indeed, ever since the Ikkō sect’s uprising, Kiyokane’s widow had repeatedly petitioned Ieyasu to rebuild the badly damaged nenbutsu halls. Her efforts had already begun to bear fruit, and the long-standing tension with the Ikkō sect had greatly eased. Ieyasu had done this, of course, as a precaution against Hideyoshi—a case of preparing for the storm before it broke.
